guide.title: Fixed spectral basis states
guide.summary: the Fourier features sum w exp(i c omega.x) of a declared frequency set, aggregated once per group as certified complex enclosures summed as exact scaled integers (CPU and CUDA bit for bit, CALC-003's certified sin / cos), phase actions answered from the fixed basis without rescanning (translations, phases, derivatives multiplying by i c omega exactly, the characteristic function), new frequencies requesting a new basis state and missing spectral support refused, never treated as zero; the Boolean case is SPEC-002's exact Walsh spectrum with its exact inverse and full 2^k cost.

SPEC-001.cpu: Native C (math_fourier.c, the per-row reduction shared with CUDA in math_fourier.h): a basis plan over an FND-004 scope (d <= 16 columns, an optional weight column, unit radian / pi / turn, a set of m distinct exact int64-rational frequency vectors, sorted for exact lookup) with 64.192 fixed-point reduction constants (radians from a 512-bit 2/pi, pi and turn units exact when dyadic) and CALC-003's proven sum scale; per counted row the angle reduced exactly in 384-bit two's complement (quadrant exact, fraction to 128 bits; exact integer angles give exact sin / cos), CALC-003's certified 120-bit sin / cos, each weighted enclosure rounded outward to integers and summed exactly in 128 bits per (group, frequency); per group the selected and counted rows and the exact weight sum. Exact bounds [lo, hi] / (2^s 10^wscale) of C and S; for one radian dimension the sums equal CALC-003's phase family bit for bit. Phase actions without rescanning: translations tau and phases phi reduced exactly from the exact frequencies and the exact doubles, derivative orders in the translation (times i c omega_j) and the phase (times i), normalization by the exact weight sum (the empirical characteristic function), all as outward-rounded complex intervals; derivative states whose exact bounds are exact transforms (rotation by i^m, omega^alpha as big rationals, the unit factor c^|alpha| reported apart). Identity: columns, weight, unit, the exact frequency set and the scope's exact descriptor; require / Retained answer subsets and build new basis states for new frequencies; a frequency outside the basis is refused. The Boolean case: 2^k Walsh frequencies over 0 / 1 columns give SPEC-002's exact W(S) and the exact histogram through SPEC-002's inverse transform with its full-domain cost; incomplete Walsh sets, non-Boolean data and inexact coefficients are refused.
SPEC-001.gpu: CUDA kernels math_fourier_gpu.cu (tr_mgpu_fourier_sums): a counts kernel (a slice of rows per work item: selected rows, counted rows and the exact weight sum per group, local while the group stays the same, one atomic add per counter, two-word 128-bit atomics for the weight sums) and a feature kernel (work item = (frequency, slice of rows): the same inline exact reduction and certified per-row enclosures as the CPU, accumulated locally per group and added with exact two-word 128-bit atomics tr_atomic_add_wide under the host's proof that no partial sum leaves 2^126); the readback is adopted natively after consistency checks; equal to the CPU bit for bit (emulated with a scrambled thread order in the tests). Actions, derivatives and the Walsh inverse run on the CPU.
budgets: Build: variables = d (<= 16), support = m frequencies (<= 2^22), states = groups x m, tensor = selected rows x m, bytes = the plan, the sums and the state (CUDA: every device copy, tr_fourier_device_bytes).

Actions: degree = |alpha| + beta with the state's (<= 64), output = requests x selected frequencies, tensor = output x (d + 1), bytes = the selected coefficients; derivative: degree, states, bytes; Walsh inverse: variables = k, tensor = 2^k, iterations = k, bytes = 40 x 2^k.

Refused before allocation: AlgebraBudgetError; UnsupportedError for d > 16, a reduction constant >= 2^64, |tau| or |phi| >= 2^62; DomainError for missing spectral support, a zero weight sum (characteristic function) or a non-Boolean Walsh inverse.
limitations: One certified 120-bit sin / cos per (row, frequency), about 2 us on the CPU (no harmonic recurrences or angle-addition reuse); frequencies are int64 rationals; at most 16 dimensions.
Actions return outward-rounded double rectangles (no exact bounds of rotations by transcendental angles); only derivative states carry exact rational transforms.
Only the feature sums run on CUDA; actions, derivatives, lookups and the Walsh inverse are CPU code.
The only inverse transform is the Boolean (Walsh) one; no general discrete Fourier inversion or band-limited reconstruction is offered, and nothing is ever reconstructed from an incomplete basis.

No FND-007 certificate is emitted: FND-007's claim kinds are row relations of a scope or polynomial laws, and a basis proves neither; its exact scaled bounds (and the Walsh case's exact points) are the results' own evidence.
